 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The 2026-27 NBA season is here! Check out our team previews , including power rankings, best- and worst-case scenarios, and fantasy advice. 
 TORONTO RAPTORS
 2025-26 finish 
 Record: 46-36 (5th in the East, lost 4-3 in first round to Cavaliers)
 Offseason moves 
 Draft: Allen Graves (No. 19), Jaden Bradley (No. 50)
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Trades: Kawhi Leonard (from Clippers), Chucky Hepburn (re-signs on two-way deal), Alijah Martin (re-signed for 2 years, $4.5 million), Kyle Anderson (1 year, $3.9 million)
 Key departures: Brandon Ingram (traded to Clippers), Gradey Dick (traded to Clippers), Sandro Mamukelashvili (signed with Lakers)
 Current roster 
 Kawhi's back. (Jon Blacker/The Canadian Press vía AP)
 (Jon Blacker/The Canadian Press via AP) Preseason Power Rankings: No. 10 
 What's exciting: Toronto ranked 23rd in isolation scoring and 29th in pick-and-roll scoring efficiency last season. What does Leonard do at an elite level? Run isolations and pick-and-rolls. He is an immediate solution to the biggest issue facing Toronto's half-court offense, which has to be music to the ears of Raptors fans. And to Scottie Barnes! There will be less on his plate now, which might lead to lower numbers, but should lead to a far more dynamic role. Barnes checks virtually every box on the floor as a scorer, cutter, and screener, and playing alongside Kawhi will put him in positions to excel in every single category.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement What's concerning: The Raptors still need a better center than Jakob Poeltl. After ranking 26th in 3-point attempts and 21st in 3-point percentage last season, it would be ideal if the Raptors had a center who can space the floor. After all, they can only play small for so long with Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles. Toronto has fewer draft assets after splurging on Kawhi, but finding an upgrade would boost the team's odds of making another Finals run. — Kevin O'Connor  
 Preseason Power Rankings: How all 30 teams stack up ahead of 2026-27 
 Preseason takeaways
 Kawhi Leonard is back and can open the playbook for the Raptors. Having him off come off pindowns or be an off-ball screener can put pressure on defenses within the Raptors attack. More importantly, the business is true: the Raptors are going to bring the smoke defensively. You can try to keep Scottie Barnes and Kawhi out of an action, but one of them is ready to help at the elbow, and the other is waiting on the block. High activity, ball pressure, communication and rotations to keep teams out of rhythm have been on display. Immanuel Quickley and RJ Barrett have been more than willing to "do their job" on both ends. Keep an eye on Collin Murray-Boyles and his growth as a 3-point shooter. — Steve Jones 
 Fantasy watch 
 I'm still bullish on Collin Murray-Boyles making a big sophomore leap. If anything happens to Immanuel Quickley, Jamal Shead is the backup to watch. He's a great passer who handles the ball well, and his per-minute stats are solid. High assist rate with low turnovers is always preferred in 9-cat formats. — Dan Titus

 Betting perspective 
 46.5 — win total

 Best case, worst case 
 Best case: No. 3 seed 
 Let the record reflect that the only reason I didn't continue the top-seed trend here among Atlantic teams is because I don't believe Kawhi will play enough regular season games to take some of my half-court and offense and shooting questions off the table. He may simply be the answer in a playoff context.
 Their elite defense and transition attack is still enough of a formula to churn out wins, especially if Barnes takes another step forward.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Worst case: Play-In Tournament 
 If this is a 40-game (or worse) campaign from Kawhi, familiar questions on the offensive end could lower their ceiling. Those, plus the overall strength of the conference, could have them in the 7-10 range. — Nekias Duncan
